properties.areaDesc: Kane, UT
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 12 at 5:52AM MDT until October 12 at 11:00AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
At 552 AM MDT, A flood wave was moving down the Paria River and
through Paria Canyon. At 430 AM the Paria River Gauge at US-89
indicated a rise of 3 feet as the flood wave passed, with an increase
in flow to 2200 CFS.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding.

SOURCE...Gauges reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Paria River from just north of US-89 to the Utah/Arizona border
including Paria Canyon.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 12 at 4:16AM MST until October 12 at 11:15AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Paria River in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 1115 AM MST /1215 PM MDT/ Tonight.

* At 416 AM MST /516 AM MDT/, a river gauge on the Paria River near
US-89 in southern Utah reported a rapid rise of 3 feet from
thunderstorms that occurred on Sunday over the Paria River. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Paria River.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Paria River.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lees Ferry and Vermilion Cliffs National Monument.

This includes the Colorado River near mile marker 0.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Lees Ferry Camp Site.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Paria River and Colorado River.
properties.instruction:
Get out of the Paria River slot canyon! Flood waters will flow down
the Paria River, reaching the confluence with the Colorado River at
Lees Ferry between 12 PM and 2 PM MST.

Get out of washes and creeks if you are camping or hiking! Flooding
is occurring or imminent and will inundate creeks and washes.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 11:15 AM MST. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 11:15 AM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in South
Carolina...

Congaree River At Carolina Eastman affecting Calhoun, Richland and
Lexington Counties.

...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in South
Carolina...

Congaree River At Congaree River at Congaree NP Near Gadsden
affecting Calhoun and Richland Counties.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Congaree River at Carolina Eastman.

* WHEN...From this evening to Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 115.0 feet, Flooding occurs in low lying areas of the
Carolina Eastman Facility and at the Congaree National Park. At
119.0 feet, Extensive flooding occurs in the Congaree National
Park. Some area farmland is flooded. Minor flooding occurs at the
Carolina Eastman Facility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:58 AM EDT Monday the stage was 111.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 114.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this morning to a crest of 120.5 feet tomorrow evening. It will
then fall below flood stage early Thursday morning.
- Flood stage is 115.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Most flooding deaths occur in vehicles. Never drive through a flooded
roadway or around barricades. Turn around, don't drown.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 715 PM EDT.
